stem: In the science of hadith, what is the isnad of a report?
options: the grade a scholar gives the report
the chain of narrators who passed it on
the wording of what the Prophet ﷺ said
the book in which the report is recorded
why: A hadith has two parts: the isnad, the chain of who told whom, and the matn, the words reported. Sahih al-Bukhari's first report opens with its chain: al-Humaydi, from Sufyan, from Yahya ibn Sa'id, back to Umar ibn al-Khattab.
source: Sahih al-Bukhari 1 (its chain); Ibn al-Salah, Muqaddimah

es.stem: En la ciencia del hadiz, ¿qué es el isnad de un relato?
options: la calificación que un sabio le da al relato
la cadena de narradores que lo transmitieron
la redacción de lo que dijo el Profeta ﷺ
el libro en el que está registrado el relato
es.why: Un hadiz tiene dos partes: el isnad, la cadena de quién se lo contó a quién, y el matn, las palabras transmitidas. El primer relato de Sahih al-Bujari empieza con su cadena: al-Humaydi, de Sufyan, de Yahya ibn Sa'id, hasta Umar ibn al-Jattab.

stem: In classical hadith science, what usually separates a hasan (good) hadith from a sahih (sound) one?
options: its narrators' memory is a little less precise
its chain has one missing link along the way
it reaches us through only a single chain
its wording goes against a more reliable report
why: A hasan hadith meets the conditions of a sahih one (connected chain, upright narrators, no hidden flaw or oddness) except that a narrator's precision of memory is somewhat lighter. A broken chain or an odd text makes a report weak, while a single chain does not. Ibn al-Salah, Muqaddimah; Ibn Hajar, Nukhbat al-Fikar.
source: Ibn al-Salah, Muqaddimah; Ibn Hajar, Nukhbat al-Fikar

es.stem: En la ciencia clásica del hadiz, ¿qué suele distinguir a un hadiz hasan (bueno) de uno sahih (sólido)?
options: sus narradores tienen memoria algo menos precisa
a su cadena le falta un eslabón en el camino
nos llega por una sola cadena de narradores
su texto contradice un relato más confiable
es.why: Un hadiz hasan cumple las condiciones de uno sahih (cadena conectada, narradores íntegros, sin defecto oculto ni rareza), salvo que la precisión de memoria de un narrador es algo menor. Una cadena rota o un texto raro hacen débil un relato; una sola cadena, no. Ibn al-Salah, Muqaddimah; Ibn Hajar, Nujbat al-Fikar.

stem: What is a hadith qudsi, a 'sacred report'?
options: a Companion's own saying about the Prophet ﷺ
a report both Bukhari and Muslim graded sound
Allah's words as related by the Prophet ﷺ
a report traced to an imam of Ahl al-Bayt
why: In a hadith qudsi the Prophet ﷺ relates words of Allah in the first person, yet it is not part of the Qur'an, as in 'O My servants, I have forbidden injustice for Myself.' Sahih Muslim 2577.

es.stem: ¿Qué es un hadiz qudsi, un 'relato sagrado'?
options: un dicho de un Compañero sobre el Profeta ﷺ
un relato que Bujari y Muslim calificaron sólido
palabras de Allah transmitidas por el Profeta ﷺ
un relato atribuido a un imán de Ahl al-Bayt
es.why: En un hadiz qudsi el Profeta ﷺ transmite palabras de Allah en primera persona, pero no forma parte del Corán, como en 'Oh, siervos Míos, Me he prohibido la injusticia a Mí mismo'. Sahih Muslim 2577.

stem: The Qur'an (5:90) forbids khamr, wine. A Sunni jurist rules that a newly made drink is forbidden too, because it shares wine's effective cause: it intoxicates. Which source of law is he using?
options: ijma', the agreement of the scholars
'urf, the custom of the local people
istihsan, a jurist's equitable choice
qiyas, analogy from a shared cause
why: Qiyas carries a ruling from a case a text addresses to a new case that shares its effective cause ('illah); intoxication is the classic example. al-Shafi'i, al-Risalah; Qur'an 5:90.

es.stem: El Corán (5:90) prohíbe el jamr, el vino. Un jurista sunita dictamina que una bebida nueva también está prohibida, porque comparte la causa efectiva del vino: embriaga. ¿Qué fuente del derecho está usando?
options: el iyma', el acuerdo de los sabios
el 'urf, la costumbre de la gente local
el istihsan, una elección por equidad
el qiyas, la analogía por causa común
es.why: El qiyas lleva el dictamen de un caso que trata un texto a un caso nuevo que comparte su causa efectiva ('illa); la embriaguez es el ejemplo clásico. al-Shafi'i, al-Risala; Corán 5:90.

stem: In Sahih al-Bukhari, the Prophet ﷺ says he would have ordered the siwak (tooth-stick) at every prayer if it were not hard on his community. In which of the five rulings do jurists place the siwak?
options: wajib, obligatory
mustahabb, recommended
mubah, simply permitted
makruh, disliked
why: He held back from making it a command, so it is not obligatory, yet he urged it; jurists class it as recommended, an established sunnah. Sahih al-Bukhari 887.

es.stem: En Sahih al-Bujari, el Profeta ﷺ dice que habría ordenado el siwak (palito para los dientes) en cada oración si no fuera difícil para su comunidad. ¿En cuál de los cinco dictámenes colocan los juristas el siwak?
options: wayib, obligatorio
mustahabb, recomendado
mubah, solo permitido
makruh, desaconsejado
es.why: Se abstuvo de convertirlo en orden, así que no es obligatorio, pero lo animó; los juristas lo clasifican como recomendado, una sunna establecida. Sahih al-Bujari 887.

stem: In the Muwatta, why does Imam Malik sometimes leave aside a sound hadith that he himself records?
options: its chain passed through narrators from Iraq
his teacher Abu Hanifa had ruled against it
the caliph in Baghdad had forbidden its use
Medina's inherited practice ran the other way
why: For Malik, the living practice of the people of Medina ('amal ahl al-Madinah), handed down from the Companions there, could outweigh a single report, as with the buyer and seller's option to cancel. Muwatta Malik, Kitab al-Buyu'.

es.stem: En el Muwatta, ¿por qué el imán Malik a veces deja de lado un hadiz sólido que él mismo registra?
options: su cadena pasaba por narradores de Irak
su maestro Abu Hanifa había dictaminado en contra
el califa en Bagdad había prohibido aplicarlo
la práctica heredada de Medina iba al revés
es.why: Para Malik, la práctica viva de la gente de Medina ('amal ahl al-Madina), heredada de los Compañeros que vivieron allí, podía pesar más que un relato aislado, como en la opción del comprador y el vendedor de anular la venta. Muwatta Malik, Kitab al-Buyu'.

stem: In the hadith of Jibril, a stranger in white questions the Prophet ﷺ. What three things does the Prophet define for him, and how does he describe ihsan?
why: Umar ibn al-Khattab narrates that the stranger asked about Islam (the pillars), iman (belief in Allah, His angels, books, messengers, the Last Day and the decree) and ihsan, to worship Allah as though you see Him, for if you do not see Him, He sees you; then about the Hour. The Prophet ﷺ later said it was Jibril. Sahih Muslim 8.

rubric.point: Names Islam, iman (faith) and ihsan as the three things defined. Two of the three counts as partly.
Describes ihsan as worshipping Allah as though you see Him, and if you do not see Him, knowing He sees you. 'Doing good' alone counts as partly.

Gives any content of the other two (the pillars for Islam, the six articles of faith for iman), mentions the question about the Hour, or that the stranger was the angel Jibril (optional, strengthens).

es.stem: En el hadiz de Yibril, un desconocido vestido de blanco interroga al Profeta ﷺ. ¿Qué tres cosas define el Profeta para él, y cómo describe el ihsan?
es.why: Umar ibn al-Jattab narra que el desconocido preguntó por el islam (los pilares), el iman (creer en Allah, Sus ángeles, libros, mensajeros, el Último Día y el decreto) y el ihsan, adorar a Allah como si lo vieras, porque si tú no lo ves, Él te ve; luego, por la Hora. Después el Profeta ﷺ dijo que era Yibril. Sahih Muslim 8.

stem: What did the Amman Message (2004) and its Three Points say about the schools of Islamic law, and about declaring other Muslims unbelievers (takfir)?
why: Scholars from Sunni, Shia and Ibadi schools affirmed that followers of the eight schools of law (Hanafi, Maliki, Shafi'i, Hanbali, Ja'fari, Zaydi, Ibadi and Zahiri), along with Ash'ari theology and true Sufism, are Muslims; that takfir of them is not permitted; and that fatwas may be issued only by qualified scholars within the schools' methods. The Amman Message (2004) and its Three Points.
source: The Amman Message (2004) and its Three Points

rubric.point: Says it recognized followers of the established schools of law, Sunni and Shia (and Ibadi), as Muslims. Naming several of the schools strengthens; 'all religions are equal' does not count.
Says it ruled out takfir, declaring followers of those schools unbelievers.
Mentions that only qualified scholars may issue fatwas, or that it was issued in Jordan and signed by scholars across schools (optional, strengthens).

es.stem: ¿Qué dijeron el Mensaje de Amán (2004) y sus Tres Puntos sobre las escuelas del derecho islámico y sobre declarar incrédulos a otros musulmanes (takfir)?
es.why: Sabios de escuelas sunitas, chiitas e ibadíes afirmaron que los seguidores de las ocho escuelas de derecho (hanafí, malikí, shafi'í, hanbalí, ya'farí, zaydí, ibadí y zahirí), junto con la teología ash'arí y el sufismo auténtico, son musulmanes; que no se permite el takfir contra ellos; y que solo los sabios calificados, dentro de los métodos de las escuelas, pueden emitir fetuas. El Mensaje de Amán (2004) y sus Tres Puntos.
